parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence; same-sex conduct decriminalised through courts with a 2019-2021 trajectory culminating in statutory deletion, showing institutions working for LGBT people. Two 2017 high-court rulings compelled gender-marker recognition — direct evidence that courts protect trans identity and the state complies when ordered. A registered community organisation operates openly; no documented trans-specific violence (though the record is dated, 2011, so the violence axis is thin rather than assessed). Detention placement, facility access and border practice are undocumented; Section 167 (women) remains unrepealed and could be a police lever, and implementation of precedents is described as unsatisfactory. Official signals are mixed (a lethal-threat politician in 2011, but presidential tolerance statements and deportation of a hate preacher). These positives with open questions, no organised targeting and no universal exposure sit in reduced risk, below jurisdictions with documented working visitor remedies.
